notes: The metro is safe and clean (Bilhete Único). Uber and 99 are cheap. Traffic is terrible between 17:00 and 20:00. Guarulhos is 45-90 minutes away; Congonhas is in the city.
December to March is summer: 30°C with afternoon downpours (flooding). Carnival is at Anhembi in February. May to October is ideal.
SAFETY: In the centre (Sé, Luz, 25 de Março), keep your wallet in front by day; it is empty at night. Don't take your phone out on the street. Paulista, Jardins and Vila Madalena are relaxed.
Pizza 80-100 BRL, pay-by-weight restaurant 50, mortadella sandwich 40, padaria breakfast 30. A 10% tip is included. Pix and cards are accepted everywhere.
MASP is free on Tuesdays and Pinacoteca on Saturdays. Paulista is pedestrianised on Sundays. Book A Casa do Porco months ahead. Visit Embu at the weekend.
Coxinha, pão de queijo (cheese bread), pastel, mortadella, feijoada (Wednesday and Saturday), caipirinha. Japanese food in Liberdade.

stops.name: MASP
stops.tips: Lina Bo Bardi's museum suspended in mid-air, with Van Gogh and Portinari on glass easels. Free on Tuesdays, and Paulista is car-free on Sundays.

stops.name: Avenida Paulista
stops.tips: The city's financial boulevard. On Sundays it is pedestrianised, with street musicians and Japan House.

stops.name: Bráz Pizzaria Paulista
stops.tips: São Paulo pizza (the world's second pizza city): thin crust, muçarela de búfala.

stops.name: Parque Trianon
stops.tips: A remnant of Atlantic forest on Paulista, with plenty of shade.

stops.name: Sesc Avenida Paulista Terrace
stops.tips: A free rooftop terrace with a city panorama, inside a cultural centre.

backups.name: Mocotó Vila Medeiros
backups.tips: A legend of northeastern Brazilian cooking. It's far out but worth it (Uber).

backups.name: Instituto Moreira Salles
backups.tips: A photography museum with a terrace on Paulista. Free entry.

stops.name: Mercado Municipal de São Paulo
stops.tips: A 1933 market with stained-glass windows. Try the mortadella sandwich (Hocca Bar, 300 g) and pastel de bacalhau (salt cod pastry), and sample exotic fruit (vendors are insistent).

stops.name: Catedral da Sé & Marco Zero
stops.tips: A neo-Gothic cathedral and the city's point zero. Nearby is Pátio do Colégio (founded 1554).

stops.name: Edifício Martinelli / Farol Santander
stops.tips: A 1929 skyscraper. Farol Santander has a viewing deck on the 26th floor and a skate ramp.

stops.name: Theatro Municipal
stops.tips: An imitation of the Paris Opera. Tours run Wednesday to Friday, on Ramos de Azevedo square.

stops.name: Edifício Copan
stops.tips: Niemeyer's wavy building with 1,160 apartments. See it from outside (the terrace may be closed), and visit Bar da Dona Onça.

backups.name: Bar da Dona Onça
backups.tips: Brazilian classics at the foot of Copan. Feijoada (black bean and pork stew) on Saturdays.

backups.name: Pinacoteca do Estado
backups.tips: A brick museum by Ramos de Azevedo with Brazilian art. Free on Saturdays, next to Luz station.

stops.name: Ibirapuera Park
stops.tips: The city's Central Park, with Niemeyer pavilions. Cycle, visit the lake and the Oca.

stops.name: Museu Afro Brasil
stops.tips: Afro-Brazilian culture inside the park: slavery and art.

stops.name: Figueira Rubaiyat
stops.tips: Steak under a giant fig tree, in the upmarket Jardins district.

stops.name: Rua Oscar Freire
stops.tips: Brazil's most luxurious street, with the Havaianas flagship store and Melissa.

stops.name: Museu da Imagem e do Som
stops.tips: A sound and image museum with pop exhibitions.

backups.name: A Casa do Porco
backups.tips: Among the world's 50 best. A pork tasting menu in the centre; book months ahead.

backups.name: Casa de Vidro
backups.tips: The architect's glass house in Morumbi. Reservation required.

stops.name: Beco do Batman
stops.tips: Batman Alley graffiti in Vila Madalena. It changes every week.

stops.name: Coffee Lab
stops.tips: A Brazilian coffee laboratory run by Isabela Raposeiras.

stops.name: Mercado de Pinheiros
stops.tips: A neighbourhood market. Try Comedoria Gonzales, Peruvian cuisine by Rodrigo Oliveira.

stops.name: Instituto Tomie Ohtake
stops.tips: Ruy Ohtake's purple and red building in Pinheiros, with free exhibitions.

stops.name: Bar São Cristóvão
stops.tips: A football-obsessed bar on Aspicuelta street, with a street party on Fridays and Saturdays.

backups.name: Feira da Praça Benedito Calixto
backups.tips: A Saturday antiques and crafts market with chorinho music.

backups.name: Bar Veloso
backups.tips: The city's best coxinha (chicken croquette) and caipirinha. Expect a queue.

stops.name: Liberdade
stops.tips: The largest Japanese community outside Japan, with red torii gates and lanterns. On Sundays there is a market at Praça da Liberdade.

stops.name: Aska Lamen
stops.tips: A small Japanese ramen shop. Expect a queue, and bring cash.

stops.name: Museu da Imigração
stops.tips: A former immigrant hostel (like Ellis Island), covering Italian, Japanese and Turkish-Syrian migration.

stops.name: Bixiga
stops.tips: Cantinas on Rua 13 de Maio, the Vai-Vai samba school, and the Nossa Senhora Achiropita festival in August.

stops.name: Cantina Famiglia Mancini
stops.tips: A cantina on Rua Avanhandava since 1980. Giant portions of pasta and a queue.

backups.name: Templo Busshinji
backups.tips: A Zen temple, as an alternative to a museum.

backups.name: Sujinho
backups.tips: A late-night steakhouse serving churrasco, open 24 hours.

stops.name: Embu das Artes
stops.tips: A colonial artists' town 27 km away. The weekend crafts market is the draw (shops only on weekdays). It's 1 hour by bus.

stops.name: Igreja Nossa Senhora do Rosário
stops.tips: A 1690 Jesuit church with a sacred art museum.

stops.name: Restaurante Os Girassóis
stops.tips: A restaurant in a colonial house serving feijoada and Minas Gerais cooking.

stops.name: Embu Antique and Rustic Furniture Shops
stops.tips: Wooden furniture and ceramics. Shipping is available.

stops.name: Parque Villa-Lobos
stops.tips: A park in western São Paulo on the way back, for sunset and cycling.

backups.name: Parque Estadual da Cantareira
backups.tips: Atlantic forest north of the city, with views from Pedra Grande. Nature instead of Embu.

backups.name: Casa do Sino
backups.tips: A cantina serving pizza and pasta.

stops.name: Parque Buenos Aires
stops.tips: A French-style garden for a neighbourhood morning.

stops.name: Padaria Santa Teresa
stops.tips: A padaria (Brazilian bakery) breakfast: pão na chapa (grilled buttered bread) and pingado (milky coffee). A farewell treat.

stops.name: Museu do Futebol
stops.tips: A football museum inside Pacaembu stadium, with Pelé and Garrincha. Interactive.

stops.name: Guarulhos International Airport
stops.tips: Uber takes 45-90 minutes in traffic. Farewell.

backups.name: Museu do Ipiranga
backups.tips: The Independence Museum, restored in 2022. Gardens, as an alternative to football.
